12.0.0.en: "Cloud": he means the heroes of faith in the Old Testament who have come to be in heaven, so he expresses them as a cloud, and also because of their multitude, like the drops of water gathered together inside a cloud.

12.0.1.en: "Witnesses": the lives of these saints bear witness to practical faith.

12.0.2.en: "Compassed about us": the stories of their lives surround us and call us to imitate them, and they intercede for us so that we may be able to continue our striving.

12.0.3.en: "Let us run": we run like racers in a running race, that is, we hasten.

12.0.4.en: Therefore, brethren Hebrews, we have a great advantage and strength from the saints of the Old Testament, as a great cloud surrounding us who are on earth, from the good things and prayers of those who went before us and who bear witness to the victorious life of faith. Since we have this great cloud from which we draw strength, come, let us lay aside every weight of fear of persecutions and anxiety, because we have seen in the cloud those who had the weight of persecution but laid it aside by faith, such as David. This cloud also gives us strength to lay aside sin, with its many enticements and its ways which may beset us to make it easy for us to be far from God, and come, let us hasten to persevere in spiritual striving.

12.1.0.en: "The author and finisher of our faith": our God, who completes our salvation and is the foundation of our faith.

12.1.1.en: "Jesus": he mentions His name in the flesh to declare that He is the Son of Man who strove as we do and endured all sufferings.

12.1.2.en: "The right hand of the throne of God": the divine glory in the heavens, for the right hand means power and glory, and the throne means honor and perfect glory.

12.1.3.en: What encourages us to spiritual striving is imitating Christ, who set a goal before Him, namely our salvation, and endured the Cross, the sign of shame and disgrace. After He accomplished our salvation He rose from the dead and ascended to the heavens, that is, He came to be in the glory, which is a crown for everyone who completes his striving in this world.

12.2.0.en: The Apostle calls us to contemplate Christ's endurance of the opposition of the wicked, who tried many times to catch Him in a word and also tried to kill Him several times until they finally crucified Him. He endured them to teach us how to endure others, and He endured the torments of the Cross to complete our salvation. And as we always think of Christ's striving for us, we do not grow weary of enduring our sufferings or grow weak in continuing the striving, but persevere with confidence until we receive the heavenly crowns.

12.2.1.en: Take care to read the Gospels and the lives of the saints, so that you may be encouraged by the life of Christ and the life of His children to continue your spiritual striving, and God will send you consolations that support you, so do not be troubled however many your sins or your tribulations.

12.3.0.en: He encourages them to continue the spiritual striving by resisting sin unto death, so that they do not surrender to it however long the time, confident of the power of God within them, which is able to defeat the wars of the devil.

12.4.0.en: You have pitied yourselves because of the chastenings to which you are exposed, not remembering what you learned from God in the Holy Bible, which exhorts you as sons, as in the Book of Proverbs (Prov 3:11): My son, do not despise the chastenings that come to you from the Lord, and do not grow weak or despair if rebuke is directed to you, for it is because of His love for you, because you are His son and He wants you in the best spiritual condition, and He allows you some sufferings as a fellowship in the cross of His beloved Son who was crucified for you and who endured many scourgings for you. So tribulations are by God's permission for the correction of our faults and the growth of our life.

12.5.0.en: If you, beloved, accept chastening from God with patience, He is caring for you as His sons, because a father who cares for his children does not neglect their weakness and faults but corrects them by chastening.

12.6.1.en: If you reject the divine chastening that came upon all the children of God in the Old Testament and in which they shared for the correction of their lives and to bring them near to God, then your persistence in rejecting chastening declares that you are not sons of God. His use of the expression "illegitimate sons" matters to the Jews, who are careful about their genealogies in order to reach God; that is, he affirms that chastening is the proof of sonship. It is noted that the phrase "whereof all are partakers" is a parenthetical phrase which means that all the children of God accept chastening, but the meaning of the verse becomes easy if we say that those who are without chastening are not children of God.

12.7.0.en: What is more, as a proof of the necessity of our submitting to God's chastening, we respect our fleshly fathers who rebuked us and punished us to correct our faults. How much more should we submit to God, the Father of our spirits in addition to our bodies, who permits trials to correct our spirits so that we may be able to live with Him and find our place in eternal life.

12.8.0.en: Our fleshly fathers chastened us for a limited period until we became grown, and this chastening was according to their own opinion, which is liable to some error. But God chastens us by tribulations that we may profit spiritually, and He is holy and does not err; so by His chastening we are sanctified like Him, and we live with Him on earth and in heaven with all the saints.

12.9.0.en: Tribulations with their sufferings cause a person sorrows, but they are temporary, and afterward they form in him virtues and spiritual fruits that remain with him forever to enjoy in the Kingdom. So chastening seems hard at its beginning, but afterward it produces peace and joy, while not accepting chastening gives a temporary pleasure and rest followed by sorrow and eternal destruction.

12.9.1.en: Trust that every tribulation you pass through is for your benefit, so do not murmur against it, but ask God's help to endure it and cling to Him more, and you will grow in your spiritual life and be happier in the end than those around you, because you are strong and your personality is more mature than many because of the tribulations you have endured.

12.10.s.en: (3) Helping the weak and guarding against sin

12.10.0.en: "The hands which hang down": the slothful.

12.10.1.en: "The feeble knees": those who despair and have lost the ability to continue the striving.

12.10.2.en: Because of the tribulations and persecutions that God permits for the chastening of His children, some fall into sloth or despair. So St. Paul the Apostle reminds them of the words of Isaiah the prophet in (Isa 35:3) that they should encourage the slothful and the despairing so that they may be strengthened and continue their striving. And of course, before supporting others, a person encourages himself to rise from his sloth or despair.

12.11.0.en: "Make straight paths for your feet": walk uprightly.

12.11.1.en: "Turned out of the way": goes astray.

12.11.2.en: "That which is lame": the weak believer.

12.11.4.en: By your sound understanding of the word of God, walk uprightly, so that those weak in faith may imitate you and not depart from the way of God, but on the contrary be delivered from their weakness and become strong in faith.

12.11.5.en: Instead of judging sinners, take care to help them correct their faults by your prayers, your good example, the expression of your love for them, and alerting them to return from their faults if you have standing with them.

12.12.0.en: Keep your peace in your dealings with others, even if this requires some concessions and care in speech, while being careful about holiness and purity, so that you are without personal motives or exploitation of others, especially since this holiness or purity is a condition for seeing God and cleaving to Him.

12.13.0.en: "Fail of the grace of God": he loses the work of God in him because of his rejection of the grace of God.

12.13.1.en: "Any root of bitterness springing up": a plant whose taste is bitter appears and grows; he means a person's deviation from the faith or his persistence in sin.

12.13.3.en: "Be defiled": stumble and fall into sin.

12.13.4.en: He calls them to care for the believers so that they may be steadfast in the Church and enjoy the grace of God in it, and none of them deviate and distress and cause the others to stumble.

12.14.0.en: He warns them against persisting in sin and making light of it, such as persisting in uncleanness even to fornication, or as Esau did when he made light of his birthright and sold it for a meal of lentils.

12.15.0.en: When Esau came to his father Isaac asking the blessing of the birthright without right, because he had sold it to his brother Jacob, he was rejected by God, who allowed his brother to take the blessing, since his regret found no effectiveness and no place for changing his position, although he sought the blessing with tears, pleading to receive it, but he could not, because he did not weep for the sake of repentance but for the sake of the lost blessing.

12.16.s.en: (4) A comparison between the glory of the two covenants

12.16.0.en: St. Paul the Apostle explains God's meeting with His people in the Old Testament to give them the commandments and the Law. He appeared in a great fire on the material, tangible mountain, and the mist was so thick that the place became dark, and a violent wind like whirlwinds surrounded the mountain, to declare the greatness of God and to establish the fear of Him in the hearts of His people.

12.17.0.en: The people heard the sound of trumpets and were afraid, and asked Moses to speak with God and then tell them, because they could not bear to see or hear the fearful God (Ex 20:19).

12.18.0.en: God said to Moses that if any animal touched the mountain it must die, and they were not to touch it after its touching the mountain, but it was to be stoned or shot through with an arrow from a distance (Ex 19:13).

12.19.0.en: Jewish tradition mentions that the sight was so frightening that Moses himself, the great prophet, "he who spoke with God," said, "I exceedingly fear and quake."

12.20.0.en: The glory of the New Testament appears in the greatness of the Kingdom of Heaven, filled with angels, and this Kingdom is of course better than Mount Zion beside Jerusalem or the earthly city of Jerusalem that the Jews hold holy, but which is merely a symbol of the Kingdom of Heaven.

12.21.1.en: "Firstborn": in the Old Testament the firstborn had special blessings, and what is meant by the firstborn is the saints who completed their striving and receive spiritual blessings that cannot be expressed.

12.21.2.en: "Written": their names are written, that is, they are established.

12.21.3.en: "The spirits of just men made perfect": saints who completed their lives by the grace of God and so reached heaven. He describes the Kingdom as an assembly of believers upon whom the grace of God abounds, established in glory around God the just Judge, who rejoices in the spirits of His children around Him and completes all their deficiencies by His grace.

12.22.0.en: "Mediator": Christ's mediating between man and God, and His making peace by His redemption of us and paying the debt for us.

12.22.1.en: "Blood of sprinkling": the blood of the blood sacrifices was sprinkled on the altar in the Old Testament, and the blood of Christ is sprinkled on us, that is, it atones for us and we receive His forgiveness through the sacraments of confession and Holy Communion.

12.22.2.en: "Speaketh better things than that of Abel": after Cain killed Abel, his blood proclaimed the sin of Cain, but the blood of Christ speaks better than Abel's, proclaiming the salvation and forgiveness of those who believe in Him.

12.22.3.en: He continues the comparison between the Old and the New Testament, showing the greatness of Christ the Redeemer as a mediator who reconciles man with God, and His blood gives salvation to His children.

12.23.0.en: "Refuse not him that speaketh": do not reject the word of Christ.

12.23.1.en: "They": the children of Israel in the days of Moses.

12.23.2.en: "Escaped not": God was angry with them, so they died in the wilderness of Sinai and did not enter the promised land. "Him that spake on earth": Moses.

12.23.4.en: He warns them against falling away from the Christian faith by returning to the customs of the Jews, because if God was angry with the children of Israel long ago in the days of Moses when they rejected His word about entering the promised land and worshipped the golden calf and fell into many murmurings, so that they perished, how much more will be the punishment of him who falls away from faith in Christ, who comes from the heavens for our salvation.

12.23.5.en: Remember that the words of the Holy Bible are words from heaven that Christ sends you every day to guide your life, so take care to apply them and let them be your goal all day long.

12.24.0.en: At the voice of God in the days of Moses the earth shook when He appeared on the mountain before all the people, and He will come once again at the second coming of Christ, and the material heaven and earth will shake and be changed, so that the new heaven and earth, that is, the Kingdom of Heaven, may remain forever.

12.25.0.en: While we prepare for the eternal Kingdom, we thank God for His grace, by which we are able to serve Him, and this service is characterized by the following:

12.25.1.en: 1- It pleases God and is not according to our own desires.

12.25.2.en: 2- With humility and the fear of God.

12.25.3.en: 3- With righteousness, goodness and doing good.

12.26.0.en: St. Paul declares the greatness and power of God, likening Him to a fire that consumes all evils and destroys those who resist, and he took this expression from (Deut 4:24). He destroys the evil that is in us when we repent, but for him who persists in evil, the eternal fire awaits.

12.26.1.en: The fear of God creates within us a rejection of sin and a distancing from its sources, and if we fall into it, we return quickly by repentance to be cleansed from it, so that we live always in purity and see God and rejoice in Him.

13.0.0.en: The Apostle calls them to love others and to continue and grow in it.

13.1.0.en: He alerts them to take care to entertain strangers, for it gives blessings to the one who does it greater than he imagines, such as Abraham and Lot, who entertained men and discovered afterward that they were angels; indeed, in the case of our father Abraham, God Himself was with the two angels (Gen 18:2; 19:1, 2).

13.2.0.en: Remember those who are in bonds, and do not be in a high tower, separated from those who are in sufferings, whether bonds of imprisonment for the sake of the word of God or bonds of sins. Remember them in your prayers and in visiting them and helping them. Likewise, care for those who suffer a trial or tribulation in their lives, putting yourselves in their place so that you feel their sufferings.

13.3.0.en: Marriage is a great sacrament in Christianity, higher in its meaning than all pagan ideas and other religions, since it is a union between the spouses accomplished by the Holy Spirit. So he requires the married to keep their conjugal relationship in a sound way and to keep away from every deviation against the commandments of God (Rom 1:26, 27) so that they do not defile their relationship. And he attacks strongly fornication and uncleanness of all kinds, because God will judge them and will destroy everyone who persists in them.

13.4.0.en: He calls them not to be attached to money, that is, to keep away from covetousness, or getting money in an unlawful way, or relying on it before God, or being distressed at its scarcity, and to put in their hearts that God gives them what suffices them as He promised in the Book of Joshua (Josh 1:5), and not to worry or fear that what they have is not enough, because God gives them their sufficiency and guarantees it, so that they trust in Him like David the prophet (Ps 118:6).

13.5.0.en: He alerts them to take care of their spiritual teachers, to provide for their needs, to submit to them, and to imitate their lives and their faith, whose reward is the joys of heaven into which they entered after their departure from this life.

13.5.1.en: May you learn from the fathers and spiritual guides at least one quality from each one, and take care about their guidance even if it opposes your purposes and mood, for it is spiritual experience and a message directed to you from God.

13.6.s.en: (2) The sacrifices of the Old and the New Testament

13.6.0.en: The Lord Jesus Christ is constant and does not change; He is yesterday in the Old Testament and the same today in the preaching of the Gospel with the grace of the New Testament, and He is the true God who abides forever.

13.7.0.en: The proof of steadfastness in God in ancient times was the eating of the Passover and the peace offerings, which were a type of the sacrifice of Christ in the New Testament, in which we are made steadfast by His grace when we partake of His most holy Body and Blood. So he alerts them not to return to eating of the animal sacrifices according to the Jewish rite, for they are Jewish teachings foreign to Christianity which declare that the sacrifice of Christ is not sufficient for salvation, so these teachings must be rejected.

13.8.0.en: The altar of the New Testament and what is offered on it, namely the Body and Blood of Christ, the priests and servants of the Jews are not permitted to eat of, because they believe that salvation is by eating the animal sacrifices and do not believe that salvation is by the blood of Christ alone, to which these sacrifices pointed.

13.9.0.en: "The camp": the place where the children of Israel lived and pitched their tents around the tabernacle of meeting.

13.9.1.en: "The gate": the gates of the city of Jerusalem. He also affirms that the sacrifices of the Old Testament were a type of the sacrifice of Christ, for on the great Day of Atonement the high priest would enter into the Holy of Holies with the blood of the sacrifice, while the sacrifice itself was burned outside the camp (Lev 16:27). It is a type of Christ, who was crucified outside Jerusalem at the place of Golgotha in order to redeem and sanctify those who believe in Him (Jn 19:20).

13.10.0.en: St. Paul calls the Christians of Jewish origin to leave the Jewish worship, whose center is Jerusalem, and to go out to the Christian worship, enduring insults from their Jewish brethren as Christ endured the shame of the Cross for us, because we ought to live with a mind of being strangers to the world and its lusts and positions, and endure tribulations in order to reach the heavenly Jerusalem, that is, the Kingdom of Heaven.

13.10.1.en: Do not be troubled by others' opposition to you in your holding fast to your prayers and your attachment to the Church or your spiritual principles that you learned from the fathers, and trust that these insults are a crown of boasting for you. Do not be angry; you may explain your principles to them if they want to hear, and if they refuse, then be silent and endure for God's sake and do not waver from your principles, as Christ endured all insults for your sake.

13.11.1.en: He calls us to new kinds of sacrifices in the New Testament which we are able to offer by the grace of Christ (Ps 51:16), and they are:

13.11.2.en: 1- The sacrifices of the lips, that is, prayers, praise and thanksgiving.

13.11.3.en: 2- The sacrifices of good works, that is, works of goodness and mercy.

13.12.s.en: (3) Caring for the guides and submitting to them

13.12.1.en: The Apostle calls them to obey the servants and spiritual guides who love them and regard their service as a responsibility before God for which they will give account, so that they serve them faithfully, because their not obeying them will weary them, and this makes God displeased with them, in addition to the fact that the guides will not be able to convey all the spiritual benefit to them.

13.13.0.en: With humility and love St. Paul, who is their father and spiritual guide, asks them to pray for him that God may give him wisdom in his service and his conduct, for he loves them and his conscience is sincere toward them. By this humility he completes the meaning of the previous verse, in which he requires them to submit to the guides, so that they would not think he wanted to lord it over them rather than seek their spiritual benefit.

13.14.0.en: He also asks for their prayers to ease his coming to them, for he longs to see them, and he feels that he is of Jewish origin and wishes to return to Jerusalem and Judea, where he lived and was taught.

13.15.0.en: "The God of peace": St. Paul was compelled in this epistle to refute the arguments of the false teachers who wanted to take the Christians back to Jewish worship, and they had opposed him greatly. Now he wishes that the believers may live in peace that God, the God of heaven, grants them, keeping away from arguing with these false teachers and from all the problems that arise with them.

13.15.1.en: "Brought again": he speaks of Christ as a man who needed God to raise Him from the dead, that is, His divinity raised His humanity. He wishes that the believers may live in peace from God, who is able to do all things, who raised Christ from the dead and who is the shepherd of our souls as a shepherd tends the sheep. And this peace helps us to concentrate on good works, which are the will of God in our lives and by which we please Him, and He helps us to complete them throughout our life and forever.

13.16.0.en: If St. Paul was compelled to refute the ideas of the false teachers and explain them in this epistle, he apologizes to the Christians of Jewish origin who read this epistle and asks their forbearance of these many words of his, which are very brief; and had he let himself explain, he would have written far more than this.

13.16.1.en: Be gentle in your speech with others, care about their feelings, and adorn yourself with words of apology and asking leave, so that you win your hearers.

13.17.0.en: Let it be known to you, beloved, that our brother Timothy, whom you know well, has been released from his prison and will be with me when I come and see you very soon, if the Lord will and we live.

13.18.0.en: He asks that his greeting be conveyed to their guides and servants, for they are responsible for the care of the Church among them, and also to all the believers to whom it may be hard to convey the epistle so that they may read it. And on the other hand he sends the greetings of all the believers around him in Italy, where he wrote this epistle.

13.19.0.en: He wishes at the close of his epistle that the grace of Christ may always work in them. And he makes clear that he dictated this epistle to Timothy when he was in Rome, which is in Italy, because his eyesight is weak and he needs someone to write his epistles for him. And he mentions Timothy his disciple because he is known and accepted among the Jews, for his mother and grandmother were Jewesses (Acts 16:1-3), and this makes their acceptance of the epistle easy.

13.19.1.en: When you use a mediator between yourself and others, take care that he is accepted and loved by them, so that agreement may be made or matters between you and them completed, for a person is affected psychologically and accepts the words if they are from someone known and loved by him.
